R01.note: Strong single write path, button-bound confirm and race tests, but history lacks currency/reason, no conversation id, no happy-path confirm test or prompt-injection-in-product-data test, and migration lock/rollback is not addressed.

R02.note: Thorough and correct on storage, confirm binding and concurrency, but the tool schema omits reason, the migration ignores locks/rollback, expired/cancelled proposals are swept away, and it runs well past ~25 bullets.

R03.note: Conditional UPDATE...WHERE status='pending' RETURNING plus revision check and good adversarial tests, but session-based role check is only implied, tool lacks reason, migration ignores locks/rollback and no conversation id or confirmer on proposals.

R04.note: Clean proposal/confirm design with stale-price 409 and idempotency, but tests do not state real Postgres, agent tests mock the API rather than the LLM with no injection case, and migration safety is thin.

R05.note: Confirmation is a typed CONFIRM after which the agent calls the confirm endpoint, which is exactly the trusted-chat-text pattern the rubric forbids; no stale-price check, no old-price snapshot or one-current-row constraint.

R06.note: Solid end to end with human-session buttons, stale check and real-Postgres tests, but the tool schema uses no decimal string, migration lock safety is absent, and agent tests mock HTTP with no LLM or injection case.

R07.note: Very strong on history, validation and concurrency, but allows an allowlisted typed phrase as consent, does not tie the role check explicitly to the session, and lacks a prompt-injection-in-product-data test.

R08.note: Best coverage of confirm binding, conditional UPDATE, session-based admin check and injection tests, but route idempotency/status codes and currency validation are vague, the tool omits reason, and migration lock/rollback is not discussed.

R09.note: Reasonable proposal and stale-price handling, but confirmation relies on a typed CONFIRM reply, no one-current-row constraint, no idempotency, no conversation id and tests do not state real Postgres.

R10.note: Concise and correct on confirm binding, session-derived admin identity and stale/idempotent confirm, but the tool takes a number rather than a decimal string, migration safety covers only backfill/down, and tests omit real Postgres and injection cases.
